column1: EduVision STQA – GUI-Reproducible Bug Register (New Findings)

column5: Question-level grade override endpoint has zero authentication
column6: QuestionEvaluationViewSet defines no permission_classes/authentication_classes, and the global DRF default is AllowAny; the override_marks action registers a live PATCH route despite the base ReadOnlyModelViewSet.
column7: Any unauthenticated actor can permanently overwrite any student's question-level marks and feedback and force score recalculation.
column8:
Precondition: Know or enumerate a QuestionEvaluation id (visible in any evaluated script's report response).
1. Log out of the application completely (or use a private browsing window with no session).
2. Open browser dev tools / Postman and send PATCH /api/evaluation/evaluations/<id>/override_marks/ with body {"method_marks_awarded": 999} and no Authorization header.
3. Observe the response returns 200 OK with the updated evaluation.
4. As a teacher, open the corresponding script's report in the GUI and confirm the marks have changed.
column9: The request should be rejected with 401 Unauthorized since no credentials were supplied.
column10: The grade override succeeds and the script totals are recalculated with no authentication check.

column5: Class/Section/Subject/Teacher/Student profile CRUD endpoints have no permission classes
column6: ClassListCreateView, SectionListCreateView, TeacherProfile and StudentProfile views, SubjectListCreateView, and TeacherSubjectAssignment views declare no permission_classes, falling back to the global AllowAny default.
column7: Any unauthenticated actor can read and write full student PII (address, guardian names/phone, blood group, DOB) and create/delete classes, sections, subjects, and teacher-subject assignments.
column8:
Precondition: None — no login required.
1. Open a private browsing window (no session cookies) and, using a REST client, send GET /api/school/students/.
2. Observe the response 200 OK with a full list of student profiles including addresses and guardian phone numbers.
3. Send PATCH /api/school/students/<user_id>/ with a modified address field.
4. Log in as the affected student in the GUI and view their profile — observe the address has changed despite no authenticated request being made.
column9: All requests without a valid Authorization header should return 401 Unauthorized.
column10: Full CRUD access is granted with no credentials.

column5: RubricSetViewSet has no permission classes — full CRUD/publish/archive unauthenticated
column6: RubricSetViewSet sets no permission_classes, relying on the global AllowAny default; the frontend rubrics API client also never attaches an Authorization header for any rubric call.
column7: Any unauthenticated actor can create, edit, delete, publish, or archive grading rubrics that directly determine how student answer scripts are scored.
column8:
Precondition: None — no login required.
1. In a private browsing window, use a REST client to send DELETE /api/rubric-sets/<id>/ for a known draft rubric set id.
2. Observe 204 No Content.
3. Log in as the owning teacher in the GUI and navigate to the Rubrics page — observe the rubric set is gone.
column9: The delete should be rejected with 401 Unauthorized.
column10: The rubric set is deleted with no authentication.

column5: Content download endpoint skips the ownership check its sibling endpoint enforces
column6: download_generated_content_view is decorated only with IsAuthenticated and never calls the _user_can_view_request() helper before serving the file, whereas the equivalent GeneratedContentView.get explicitly checks it.
column7: Any authenticated user can download any other user's generated PDF/worksheet content by supplying an arbitrary request_id in the URL.
column8:
Precondition: Log in as Student A; know or enumerate a request_id UUID belonging to Student B (e.g. from network traffic or a shared class discussion).
1. Log in as Student A in the GUI.
2. Using browser dev tools, send GET /api/content-requests/<Student B's request_id>/download/?format=pdf with Student A's Bearer token.
3. Observe the response is 200 OK and returns Student B's generated worksheet file.
column9: The response should be 404 Not Found since Student A does not own that content request.
column10: The file downloads successfully regardless of ownership.

column5: Student role bypasses answer-script scoping in AnswerScriptViewSet
column6: AnswerScriptViewSet.get_queryset() only applies a scoping filter when user.role == "teacher"; for the student role the branch is skipped entirely and the unfiltered queryset is returned as-is.
column7: Any authenticated student can list and view every student's uploaded answer scripts, grades, feedback, and identified mistakes via the generic scripts endpoint, not just their own.
column8:
Precondition: Log in as a student account.
1. Log in as any student.
2. Using dev tools with the student's Bearer token, send GET /api/evaluation/scripts/.
3. Observe the response includes answer scripts belonging to other students across other sections, including scores and feedback.
4. Send GET /api/evaluation/scripts/<other student's script id>/report/ and observe full grading detail is returned.
column9: A student querying this endpoint should see only their own scripts (or receive 403 Forbidden).
column10: All scripts in the system are returned regardless of ownership.

column5: Rotated refresh tokens are never blacklisted allowing replay after rotation or logout
column6: SIMPLE_JWT sets ROTATE_REFRESH_TOKENS: True but rest_framework_simplejwt.token_blacklist is absent from INSTALLED_APPS, and LogoutView/RefreshView only clear/rotate the cookie client-side without invalidating the old token server-side.
column7: A stolen or previously-issued refresh token remains valid for its full 7-day lifetime even after the legitimate user logs out or the token is rotated.
column8:
Precondition: Capture the refresh_token cookie value via browser dev tools after logging in.
1. Log in normally and copy the refresh_token cookie value from DevTools > Application > Cookies.
2. Click Logout in the GUI.
3. Using a REST client, POST to /api/auth/refresh/ sending the captured (logged-out) cookie value directly.
4. Observe a new valid access token is still issued.
column9: The refresh token should be rejected after logout since the session was terminated.
column10: The old refresh token continues to mint new access tokens.

column5: Study plan and study plan item detail/update/delete actions bypass user-scoped queryset
column6: StudyPlanViewSet.list() and StudyPlanItemViewSet.list() correctly scope by user, but retrieve/partial_update/destroy/add_item/mark_complete/link_request all fetch the object via get_object_or_404 directly, bypassing the ownership filter entirely.
column7: Any authenticated user can view, edit, delete, mark-complete, or attach content-request links to another user's private study plan and its items by supplying a known/guessed id.
column8:
Precondition: Log in as User A and User B in two separate browser sessions; User B has created a study plan.
1. As User B, create a study plan via the Study Plans page and note its id from the network response.
2. As User A, open dev tools and send DELETE /study-plans/<User B's plan id>/.
3. Observe 204 No Content.
4. As User B, refresh the Study Plans page — observe the plan has disappeared.
column9: User A's request should return 404 Not Found since the plan does not belong to them.
column10: User A can delete (or edit/complete) User B's study plan.

column5: Learning context endpoint has no ownership check on content_request_id
column6: LearningContextView.post/.get only requires IsAuthenticated and never verifies that request_id belongs to request.user before reading or writing personalization context data.
column7: Any authenticated user can read or overwrite another user's personalization inputs (weaknesses/goals/notes) for any content request by guessing its UUID.
column8:
Precondition: Know another user's content request id (e.g. from a shared classroom discussion or network capture).
1. Log in as an unrelated user.
2. Send POST /api/content-requests/<other user's request_id>/context/ with {"notes": "tampered"}.
3. Observe 200 OK/201 Created.
4. As the content request's real owner, open the content generation flow and observe the learning context notes have been overwritten.
column9: The request should return 403 Forbidden/404 Not Found for a request_id the caller does not own.
column10: The context is read/overwritten with no ownership validation.

column5: Topic progress update and difficulty flagging accept any topic id with no enrollment check
column6: progress_service.update_topic_progress and difficulty_service.flag_topic fetch the CourseTopic by raw pk and write progress/difficulty data without calling the enrollment check (_can_view_outline) that guards the read-side endpoints.
column7: Any authenticated student can mark topics from courses they are not enrolled in as completed or flag them as difficult, polluting another section's teacher-facing analytics.
column8:
Precondition: Log in as a student who is not enrolled in Course X's section; know a topic_id belonging to Course X.
1. Log in as the unrelated student.
2. Send POST /api/curriculum/topics/<Course X topic_id>/progress/ with {"status": "completed"}.
3. Observe 200 OK.
4. As the teacher of Course X, open the Difficulty Report / progress dashboard and observe the unrelated student's progress entry appears for a course they never enrolled in.
column9: The request should be rejected with 403 Forbidden since the student is not enrolled in that course's section.
column10: The progress/flag record is created for any topic id regardless of enrollment.

column5: Handwriting-to-LaTeX and equation-solver endpoints are completely unauthenticated
column6: convert_to_latex and evaluate_equation are plain csrf_exempt Django function views that bypass the DRF permission stack entirely, and the frontend calls them with no Authorization header or credentials.
column7: Any unauthenticated actor can repeatedly invoke the paid Gemini Vision API through these endpoints with no rate limiting or auth check.
column8:
Precondition: None — no login required.
1. In a private browsing window with no session, use a REST client to POST a base64 PNG image to /api/whiteboard/convert/ with {"image": "data:image/png;base64,...", "type": "math"}.
2. Observe 200 OK with a LaTeX conversion result returned, with no authentication performed.
3. Script repeated calls in a loop to observe no throttling kicks in.
column9: The endpoint should require authentication and apply rate limiting.
column10: Unlimited unauthenticated access to the AI conversion feature is possible.

column5: DEBUG defaults to True and a hardcoded SECRET_KEY ships as the fallback when env vars are unset
column6: SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded value checked into source control, and DEBUG defaults to "True" when the environment variable is unset.
column7: A misconfigured production deployment exposes full Django debug tracebacks (source code
column9: SQL) and uses a guessable secret key that can forge session/signed data.
column10:
Precondition: Deploy the backend without setting DEBUG or SECRET_KEY environment variables (the documented default path).
1. Start the Django server with no .env file or with those two variables unset.
2. In a browser, navigate to any URL that triggers a server error (e.g., malformed UUID in a detail URL).
3. Observe the full Django debug error page with source snippets and settings values is rendered to the browser.
column11: Production deployments should fail closed (DEBUG off
column12: no default secret) rather than silently defaulting to insecure values.
column13: The app boots in debug mode with a hardcoded secret whenever env vars are omitted.

column5: Learning event and recommendation endpoints leak all users' data absent an explicit user_id filter
column6: LearningEventViewSet.get_queryset() and RecommendationViewSet.get_queryset() only filter when a user_id query parameter is present; when omitted the full unfiltered queryset is returned, and any supplied user_id is accepted with no check that it matches request.user.id.
column7: Any authenticated user can retrieve every user's learning event history or view another specific user's topic/recommendation data by passing an arbitrary user_id.
column8:
Precondition: Log in as any authenticated user (student or teacher).
1. Log in as Student A.
2. Using dev tools, send GET /api/learning-events/ with Student A's Bearer token and no user_id query parameter.
3. Observe the response contains learning events for multiple different user_id values, not just Student A's own.
4. Send GET /api/learning-events/topics/?user_id=<Student B's id> and observe Student B's topic history is returned to Student A.
column9: Only the requesting user's own events/recommendations should ever be returned regardless of query parameters supplied.
column10: Full cross-user data is exposed when no filter is given and arbitrary user_id impersonation is accepted when one is given.

column5: Public registration endpoint crashes with 500 on duplicate username instead of returning a validation error
column6: RegisterSerializer has no validate_username/validate_email uniqueness checks, so a duplicate username raises IntegrityError inside .save(); RegisterView.post catches this in a bare except Exception, but DRF re-raises non-APIException errors, producing an unhandled 500.
column7: Users attempting to register with a taken username receive a generic server error instead of an actionable message; email also has no uniqueness enforcement, allowing duplicate accounts by email.
column8:
Precondition: /api/auth/register/ is reachable (no GUI form exists, but the endpoint is live and unauthenticated).
1. Using a REST client, POST /api/auth/register/ with a new username/email and valid password fields — confirm 201 Created.
2. Repeat the exact same POST body a second time.
3. Observe the response is 500 Internal Server Error with a raw traceback-style error rather than a validation message.
column9: A 400 Bad Request with {"username": "already exists"} should be returned.
column10: An unhandled IntegrityError propagates into a 500 response.

column5: Regenerate endpoint's ownership check is skipped when the original creator was deleted
column6: RegenerateContentView.post guards ownership with "if original.created_by_id and original.created_by_id != request.user.id", but created_by uses on_delete=SET_NULL; once the original creator's account is deleted, created_by_id becomes None and the check is skipped entirely.
column7: After a teacher or student account is deleted any other authenticated user can trigger regeneration of that orphaned user's old content requests consuming AI generation quota.
column8:
Precondition: An admin has deleted a user who previously created at least one content request (via Admin > Users > Delete).
1. As Admin, delete a teacher account that has existing content requests.
2. Log in as an unrelated student/teacher account.
3. Using dev tools, send POST /api/content-requests/<orphaned_request_id>/regenerate/.
4. Observe 201 Created is returned and a new generation job is enqueued.
column9: The request should be rejected since the caller has no relationship to the orphaned content request.
column10: Regeneration succeeds for any authenticated caller.

column5: No throttling/rate limiting configured on any endpoint including login
column6: The REST_FRAMEWORK settings define no DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES/DEFAULT_THROTTLE_RATES, and no view in the codebase sets throttle_classes, including LoginView.
column7: The login endpoint and all other API endpoints have no protection against brute-force credential guessing or scripted abuse.
column8:
Precondition: None.
1. Open the Sign In page.
2. Using a REST client, script 50+ rapid POST /api/auth/login/ requests with an incorrect password for a known username.
3. Observe none of the requests are throttled or blocked — each returns a normal 400 validation error with no 429 Too Many Requests at any point.
column9: After a threshold of failed attempts the endpoint should return 429 Too Many Requests or lock the account temporarily.
column10: Unlimited login attempts are permitted indefinitely.
